overview.title: The classic lake outing from Ifrane
overview.p1: Dayet Aoua is one of the best-known lakes near Ifrane. The shore invites a slow walk, birdwatching and views of the surrounding hills. Water levels change with the season; even when low, the setting remains a peaceful contrast to the imperial cities below the Atlas.
overview.p2: Bring water and a wind layer. A car or organised transfer is the usual way from Ifrane town.

food.title: Eating near Dayet Aoua
food.p1: Facilities at the lake are limited. Plan a picnic or eat in Ifrane before or after your visit.
food.p2: Do not rely on restaurants at the shore — bring what you need and take litter back.
food.li4: Seasonal stalls may appear — quality varies.
food.li5: Leave no litter at the lake.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Short drive from Ifrane; confirm the road condition after rain or snow.

2.title: Wildlife
2.desc: Observe birds quietly; do not feed animals.

3.title: Footwear
3.desc: Paths can be muddy — closed shoes recommended.

q1.question: How far from Ifrane?
q1.answer: A short drive — typically under 30 minutes depending on the route.

q2.question: Can I swim?
q2.answer: It is mainly a nature stop; respect local rules and water quality rather than treating it as a swimming resort.

q3.question: Best season?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn for mild weather; summer is popular for the cool air.

q4.question: Need a guide?
q4.answer: Not for a simple shore walk.

q5.question: Combine with cedars?
q5.answer: Yes — a classic Ifrane nature day.
